claims.claim: Increased phosphorylated extracellular signal-regulated kinase-positive cells were mostly CeA-SST cells in muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Moreover, increased pERK-positive cells were mostly CeA-SST cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, C, D).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, C, and D.

claims.claim: Bath application of clozapine-N-oxide inhibited spontaneous firing in hM4Di-expressing SST neurons.
claims.source: Whole-cell current-clamp recordings from acute amygdala slices prepared from the mice expressing the hM4Di in the CeA demonstrated that bath application of clozapine-N-oxide (CNO; 5 µM) inhibited spontaneous firing in the hM4Di-expressing SST neurons (Figure 4C1).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 4C1.

claims.claim: Clozapine-N-oxide had no effect on the firing of SST neurons that only expressed mCherry.
claims.source: In contrast, CNO had no effect on the firing of the SST neurons, which only expressed mCherry (Figure 4C2).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 4C2.

claims.claim: Silencing CeA-SST neurons during the primed state prevented the development of muscle pain in hM4Di-expressing mice.
claims.source: Silencing the CeA-SST neurons during the primed state prevented the development of MP in the hM4Di-expressing mice compared to the mCherry-expressing mice (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: Activation of CeA-SST neurons following peripheral injury is necessary for pain chronification.
claims.source: This result suggests that activation of the CeA-SST neurons following peripheral injury was necessary for pain chronification.
claims.evidence: This statement is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: Inhibiting CeA-SST neurons in muscle pain mice 2 weeks following muscle pain induction increased the paw withdrawal threshold on day 15.
claims.source: We found that inhibiting the CeA-SST neurons in the MP mice 2 weeks following MP induction was still effective in increasing the PW threshold on day 15 (Figure 4E)
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: The pain-reduction effect of inhibiting CeA-SST neurons lasted for 24 hours and persisted if clozapine-N-oxide was administered repeatedly.
claims.source: We found that inhibiting the CeA-SST neurons in the MP mice 2 weeks following MP induction was still effective in increasing the PW threshold on day 15 (Figure 4E), and the pain-reduction effect lasted for 24 hr and persisted if CNO was administered repeatedly (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: hM4Di-expressing muscle pain mice spent more time in the open arms during the elevated plus maze test compared to mCherry-expressing muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Compared to the mCherry-MP mice, the hM4Di-MP mice spent more time in the open arms during the EPM test (Figure 4F)
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: hM4Di-expressing muscle pain mice exhibited increased transitions between light and dark zones in the light/dark box test compared to mCherry-expressing muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Compared to the mCherry-MP mice, the hM4Di-MP mice spent more time in the open arms during the EPM test (Figure 4F), exhibited increased transitions between light and dark zones in the L/D box test (Figure 4G)
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4G.

claims.claim: hM4Di-expressing muscle pain mice buried fewer marbles in the marble burying test compared to mCherry-expressing muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Compared to the mCherry-MP mice, the hM4Di-MP mice spent more time in the open arms during the EPM test (Figure 4F), exhibited increased transitions between light and dark zones in the L/D box test (Figure 4G), buried fewer marbles in the marble burying test (Figure 4H)
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4H.

claims.claim: hM4Di-expressing muscle pain mice immobilized less in the forced swim test compared to mCherry-expressing muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Compared to the mCherry-MP mice, the hM4Di-MP mice spent more time in the open arms during the EPM test (Figure 4F), exhibited increased transitions between light and dark zones in the L/D box test (Figure 4G), buried fewer marbles in the marble burying test (Figure 4H), and immobilized less in the FST (Figure 4I).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4I.

claims.claim: hM4Di-expressing muscle pain mice spent more time in the social zone in the three-chamber sociability test compared to mCherry-expressing muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Moreover, the hM4Di-MP mice spent more time in the social zone in the three-chamber sociability test (Figure 4J).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4J.

claims.claim: The total travel distances of mCherry-expressing and hM4Di-expressing muscle pain mice were not significantly different in behavioral tests.
claims.source: However, the total travel distances of the mCherry-MP and hM4Di-MP mice were not significantly different (Figure 4F, G and J).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by behavioral data shown in Figures 4F, 4G, and 4J.

claims.claim: Chemogenetic inhibition of CeA-SST neurons in control mice had little effects on paw withdrawal threshold and behavioral performances.
claims.source: Notably, chemogenetic inhibition of the CeA-SST neurons in the hM4Di-Ctrl mice had little effects on the PW threshold and on their respective performances in the EPM, L/D box, marble burying test, FST, and sociability test (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: Inactivating CeA-SST neurons selectively reduced pain and alleviated anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Collectively, these observations suggest that inactivating the CeA-SST neurons selectively reduced pain and alleviated the anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in the MP mice.
claims.evidence: This statement is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figures 4E-J.

claims.claim: Bath application of clozapine-N-oxide selectively enhanced spontaneous firing in hM3Dq-expressing CeA-PKCδ neurons.
claims.source: Whole-cell current-clamp recordings demonstrated that bath application of CNO (5 μM) selectively enhanced spontaneous firing in the hM3Dq-expressing CeA-PKCδ neurons as compared to the mCherry-expressing CeA-PKCδ neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 4C).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4C.

claims.claim: Activation of hM3Dq-expressing CeA-PKCδ neurons greatly increased the paw withdrawal threshold in muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Like the silencing of the hM4Di-expressing CeA-SST neurons, the activation of the hM3Dq-expressing CeA-PKCδ neurons greatly increased the PW threshold in the MP mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 4D).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4D.

claims.claim: Enhancing CeA-PKCδ neurons had little effect on anxiety-like behaviors in muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Intriguingly, unlike the results of inactivating the CeA-SST neurons, enhancing the CeA-PKCδ neurons had little effect on the anxiety-like behaviors. There were no changes in the open-arm time (Figure 4—figure supplement 4E), number of transitions during the L/D box test (Figure 4—figure supplement 4F), and number of buried marbles (Figure 4—figure supplement 4G).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4E-G.

claims.claim: Enhancing CeA-PKCδ neurons did not improve depression-like behavior in muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Similarly, enhancing the CeA-PKCδ neurons did not improve depression-like behavior (Figure 4—figure supplement 4H) and sociability (Figure 4—figure supplement 4I).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4H.

claims.claim: Enhancing CeA-PKCδ neurons did not improve sociability in muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Similarly, enhancing the CeA-PKCδ neurons did not improve depression-like behavior (Figure 4—figure supplement 4H) and sociability (Figure 4—figure supplement 4I).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4I.

claims.claim: Activation of CeA-PKCδ neurons is sufficient to reduce mechanical hyperalgesia in muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Taken together, these results suggest that activation of the CeA-PKCδ neurons is sufficient to reduce mechanical hyperalgesia in the MP mice.
claims.evidence: This statement is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4D.

claims.claim: Changes in the excitability of CeA-PKCδ neurons were not causally related to muscle pain-related affective behaviors.
claims.source: However, changes in the excitability of the CeA-PKCδ neurons were not causally related to MP-related affective behaviors.
claims.evidence: This statement is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4E-I.

claims.claim: Bath application of pregabalin decreased the amplitude of light-evoked excitatory postsynaptic currents in some CeA-SST neurons of both control and muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Bath application of PGB (500 µM) decreased the amplitude of light-evoked EPSCs in some CeA-SST neurons of both the Ctrl and MP mice (Figure 5B and D).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figures 5B and 5D.

claims.claim: The percentage of neurons that were sensitive to pregabalin inhibition was increased in muscle pain mice.
claims.source: The percentage of neurons that were sensitive to PGB inhibition was increased in the MP mice (Figure 5C, left)
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: The degree of pregabalin inhibition between control and muscle pain groups was similar.
claims.source: The percentage of neurons that were sensitive to PGB inhibition was increased in the MP mice (Figure 5C, left), although the degree of inhibition between these two groups was similar (Figure 5C, right).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: The reduction of excitatory postsynaptic currents by pregabalin was concomitant with an increase in the paired-pulse ratio.
claims.source: Consistent with the presynaptic effect of PGB on α2δ VGCC subunits, the reduction of EPSCs was concomitant with an increase in the paired-pulse ratio (the interpulse interval = 200 ms; Figure 5E).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 5E.

claims.claim: Similar effects of pregabalin on synaptic transmission were found at the parabrachial nucleus to CeA-PKCδ neuron synapses.
claims.source: Similar effects of PGB on synaptic transmission were found at the PBN to CeA-PKCδ neuron synapses (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: After intraperitoneal injection of pregabalin, CeA-SST neurons exhibited decreased calcium event frequency.
claims.source: After intraperitoneal injection of PGB, the CeA-SST neurons exhibited decreased calcium event frequency (Figure 5G and H, left)
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by in vivo calcium imaging data shown in Figures 5G and 5H.

claims.claim: After intraperitoneal injection of pregabalin, CeA-SST neurons exhibited decreased mean amplitude of calcium events.
claims.source: After intraperitoneal injection of PGB, the CeA-SST neurons exhibited decreased calcium event frequency (Figure 5G and H, left) and mean amplitude (ΔF/F; Figure 5G and H, right).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by in vivo calcium imaging data shown in Figures 5G and 5H.

claims.claim: Approximately 56% of CeA-SST neurons were inhibited by pregabalin application.
claims.source: The analysis of the area under the curve (AUC) of spontaneous calcium activities suggested that approximately 56% (26/46 cells) of CeA-SST neurons were inhibited, 11% (5/46 cells) of CeA-SST neurons were excited, and 33% of (15/46 cells) CeA-SST neurons were insensitive to PGB application (Figure 5I and J).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by in vivo calcium imaging data shown in Figures 5I and 5J.

claims.claim: Approximately 11% of CeA-SST neurons were excited by pregabalin application.
claims.source: The analysis of the area under the curve (AUC) of spontaneous calcium activities suggested that approximately 56% (26/46 cells) of CeA-SST neurons were inhibited, 11% (5/46 cells) of CeA-SST neurons were excited, and 33% of (15/46 cells) CeA-SST neurons were insensitive to PGB application (Figure 5I and J).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by in vivo calcium imaging data shown in Figures 5I and 5J.

claims.claim: Approximately 33% of CeA-SST neurons were insensitive to pregabalin application.
claims.source: The analysis of the area under the curve (AUC) of spontaneous calcium activities suggested that approximately 56% (26/46 cells) of CeA-SST neurons were inhibited, 11% (5/46 cells) of CeA-SST neurons were excited, and 33% of (15/46 cells) CeA-SST neurons were insensitive to PGB application (Figure 5I and J).
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by in vivo calcium imaging data shown in Figures 5I and 5J.

claims.claim: Pregabalin suppressed glutamate transmission onto CeA-SST neurons, thereby reducing mechanical allodynia and reversing anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Taken together, these results suggest that PGB suppressed glutamate transmission onto the CeA-SST neurons, thereby reducing mechanical allodynia and reversed anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in the MP mice.
claims.evidence: This statement is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figures 5 and earlier behavioral data.

claims.claim: The acid-induced muscle pain model developed by Sluka et al., 2001 is a generally accepted preclinical animal model for chronic musculoskeletal pain syndrome.
claims.source: This model developed by Sluka et al., 2001 is a generally accepted preclinical animal model for chronic musculoskeletal pain syndrome.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the original model description.

claims.claim: The second acidic saline injection during hyperalgesic priming promoted pain chronification.
claims.source: The second acidic saline injection during the hyperalgesic priming promoted pain chronification.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Local pregabalin application into the CeA reduced mechanical allodynia and reversed affective behaviors in muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Local PGB application into the CeA reduced mechanical allodynia and reversed affective behaviors in the MP mice.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1E and 2B-E.

claims.claim: Intra-CeA pregabalin application immediately following the second acidic saline injection prevented the chronification of pain.
claims.source: Intriguingly, intra-CeA PGB application or selective inactivation of CeA-SST neurons immediately following the second acidic saline injection prevented the chronification of pain.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: Muscle pain was accompanied by enhanced glutamatergic transmission onto CeA-SST neurons.
claims.source: Notably, the MP was accompanied by enhanced glutamatergic transmission onto the CeA-SST neurons and decreased synaptic transmission onto the CeA-PKCδ neurons.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Muscle pain was accompanied by decreased synaptic transmission onto CeA-PKCδ neurons.
claims.source: Notably, the MP was accompanied by enhanced glutamatergic transmission onto the CeA-SST neurons and decreased synaptic transmission onto the CeA-PKCδ neurons.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: CeA-SST neuron excitability was increased in muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Furthermore, the CeA-SST neuron excitability and CeA-PKCδ neuron excitability was increased and decreased, respectively.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3F and 3H.

claims.claim: CeA-PKCδ neuron excitability was decreased in muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Furthermore, the CeA-SST neuron excitability and CeA-PKCδ neuron excitability was increased and decreased, respectively.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3G and 3H.

claims.claim: Chemogenetic inactivation of CeA-SST neurons effectively alleviated muscle pain and comorbid affective behaviors.
claims.source: In agreement with the role of CeA-SST neurons in central sensitization, chemogenetic inactivation or pharmacological suppression of the CeA-SST neurons by PGB effectively alleviated MP and comorbid affective behaviors.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4E-J.

claims.claim: Pharmacological suppression of CeA-SST neurons by pregabalin effectively alleviated muscle pain and comorbid affective behaviors.
claims.source: In agreement with the role of CeA-SST neurons in central sensitization, chemogenetic inactivation or pharmacological suppression of the CeA-SST neurons by PGB effectively alleviated MP and comorbid affective behaviors.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1E, 2B-E, and 5.

claims.claim: The effect of pregabalin on paw withdrawal threshold and emotional behaviors in the muscle pain mouse model may be caused by distinct simultaneously occurring circuit mechanisms.
claims.source: Therefore, the effect of PGB on the PW threshold and emotional behaviors in the MP mouse model may be caused by distinct simultaneously occurring circuit mechanisms.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on inference from the observation that PGB effects on pain and affect may be dissociable.

claims.claim: No positive correlation was observed between the increase in paw withdrawal threshold and the reduction of immobility time after pregabalin application.
claims.source: After PGB application, no positive correlation was observed between the increase in the PW threshold and the reduction of the immobility time.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Only a weak positive correlation between the change of paw withdrawal threshold and change in the number of buried marbles was detected after pregabalin application.
claims.source: On the other hand, only a weak positive correlation between the change of PW threshold and change in the number of buried marbles was detected (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Pregabalin may alleviate mechano-sensitivity and emotional behavior through different subtypes of CeA-SST neurons or distinct circuit mechanisms.
claims.source: These results indicate that PGB may alleviate the mechano-sensitivity and emotional behavior through different subtypes of the CeA-SST neurons or distinct circuit mechanisms (Figure 4—figure supplement 5; see Discussion).
claims.evidence: This statement is based on inference from the correlation data and is speculative.

claims.claim: Synaptic modifications and changes of intrinsic excitability play a crucial role in health and disease.
claims.source: Synaptic modifications and changes of intrinsic excitability play a crucial role in health and disease (Bliss et al., 2014; Fu et al., 2008; Ikeda et al., 2007; Kuner and Flor, 2016; Penzo et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: The formation of long-term potentiation at synapses in pain-related brain regions is considered one of the synaptic mechanisms underlying the transition of acute to chronic muscle pain.
claims.source: The formation of long-term potentiation at the synapses in pain-related brain regions is considered one of the synaptic mechanisms underlying the transition of acute to chronic MP (Min et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: The protein kinase C-extracellular signal-regulated kinase pathway plays a key role in the maladaptive changes in the neural circuitry of muscle pain mice.
claims.source: The protein kinase C (PKC)-extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) pathway plays a key role in the maladaptive changes in the neural circuitry of the MP mice (Chen et al., 2010; Cheng et al., 2011; Min et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Muscle pain is associated with enhanced phosphorylated extracellular signal-regulated kinase expression in the paraventricular thalamus and central nucleus of the amygdala.
claims.source: For instance, MP is associated with enhanced pERK expression in the paraventricular thalamus (PVT) and CeA (Chen et al., 2010; Cheng et al., 2011; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research and experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The paraventricular thalamus is a structure that is readily activated by both physical and psychological stressors and projects to the central nucleus of the amygdala.
claims.source: The PVT, a structure that is readily activated by both physical and psychological stressors, projects to the CeA (Penzo et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: Inhibition of protein kinase C or extracellular signal-regulated kinase activity in the paraventricular thalamus prevents the chronification of pain.
claims.source: First, inhibition of the PKC or ERK activity in the PVT, a major input to the CeA, prevents the chronification of pain (Chen et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: Upregulation of AMPA receptors function at the parabrachial nucleus-capsular central amygdala neuron synapse in muscle pain mice requires the activation of the protein kinase C-mitogen-activated protein kinase-extracellular signal-regulated kinase pathway.
claims.source: Second, upregulation of α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptors function at the PBN-capsular central amygdala neurons (CeAC) synapse in the MP mice requires the activation of the PKC-mitogen-activated protein kinase (MEK)-ERK pathway in the CeAC neurons (Cheng et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: Protein kinase C-dependent, but extracellular signal-regulated kinase-independent, enhancement of synaptic release occurs at the parabrachial nucleus-capsular central amygdala synapses in muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Finally, PKC-dependent, but ERK-independent, enhancement of synaptic release occurs at the PBN-CeAC synapses in the MP mice (Cheng et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: The excitatory postsynaptic currents and paired-pulse ratio at the parabrachial nucleus-CeA-SST neuron synapses were not significantly altered in muscle pain mice compared to control mice.
claims.source: The EPSCs and PPR at the PBN-CeA-SST neuron synapses were not significantly altered in the MP mice compared to the Ctrl mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 2)
claims.evidence: This claim is directly supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Other possible inputs may contribute to increased spontaneous synaptic events in CeA-SST neurons in muscle pain mice.
claims.source: The EPSCs and PPR at the PBN-CeA-SST neuron synapses were not significantly altered in the MP mice compared to the Ctrl mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), suggesting other possible inputs, which may contribute to increased spontaneous synaptic events.
claims.evidence: This statement is an inference based on the observation that PBN input alone does not explain the increased sEPSC frequency.

claims.claim: The central nucleus of the amygdala receives nociceptive inputs from the dorsal horn via the parabrachial nucleus and affect-related information from the basolateral amygdala.
claims.source: The CeA receives nociceptive inputs from the dorsal horn via the PBN and affect-related information from the basolateral amygdala (BLA) (Ikeda et al., 2007; Kuner and Kuner, 2021; Li and Sheets, 2020; Wilson et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Synaptic inputs from the paraventricular thalamus and basolateral amygdala onto the central nucleus of the amygdala are strengthened in chronic pain conditions.
claims.source: Previous studies have reported that synaptic inputs from the PVT and BLA onto the CeA are strengthened in chronic pain conditions (Ikeda et al., 2007; Liang et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: The paraventricular thalamus input most likely contributes to the enhancement of glutamate release to CeA-SST neurons in muscle pain mice.
claims.source: Considering the role of ERK in the PVT for MP (Chen et al., 2010), the PVT input most likely contributes to the enhancement of glutamate release to the CeA-SST neurons in the MP mice.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on inference from prior research and the current findings.

claims.claim: The contribution of the basolateral amygdala input to enhanced glutamate release to CeA-SST neurons cannot be excluded.
claims.source: Moreover, we cannot exclude the contribution of the BLA input, because BLA-CeA synapses are potentiated in chronic neuropathic pain (Ikeda et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This statement is based on inference from prior research.

claims.claim: Extracellular signal-regulated kinase is probably involved in cell-intrinsic mechanisms that increase neuronal excitability of CeA-SST neurons in muscle pain mice.
claims.source: In addition to synaptic plasticity, ERK is probably involved in the cell-intrinsic mechanisms. Considering that pERK is increased in CeA-SST neurons in the MP mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), we speculate that the ERK activity may contribute to the increase in intrinsic neuronal excitability of the CeA-SST neurons in the MP mice.
claims.evidence: This statement is speculative based on the observation of increased pERK in CeA-SST neurons.

claims.claim: The CaMKII-PKA/PKC-ERK-CREB pathway triggers gene transcription and protein synthesis.
claims.source: The CaMKII-PKA/PKC-ERK-cAMP response element binding protein (CREB) pathway triggers gene transcription and protein synthesis (Kolch, 2000).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: Activated ERK1/2 can undergo phosphorylation after translocating to the nucleus and then activate the downstream transcriptional factor CREB.
claims.source: The activated ERK1/2 can undergo phosphorylation after translocating to the nucleus and then activate the downstream transcriptional factor CREB (Iyengar et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: Activation of CREB triggers gene transcription and plasticity including regulation of a variety of ion channels, thereby changing the action potential threshold and neuronal excitability.
claims.source: Activation of CREB triggers gene transcription and plasticity including regulation of a variety of ion channels, thereby changing the AP threshold and neuronal excitability (Dong et al., 2006; Zhou et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Downregulation of A-type K+ channels or upregulation of voltage-gated Na channels can either decrease the rheobase or increase action potential numbers.
claims.source: For instance, downregulation of A-type K+ channels such as Kv4.2 expression or upregulation of the voltage-gated Na channels such as Nav1.3 and Nav1.7 expressions can either decrease the rheobase or increase action potential numbers (Bennett et al., 2019; Hu and Gereau, 2003).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: In a neuropathic pain model, neuropathic pain-induced activated forms of ERK and cFos were preferentially expressed in CeA-PKCδ neurons.
claims.source: A recent study by Wilson et al., 2019, demonstrated that neuropathic pain-induced activated forms of ERK (pERK) and cFos were preferentially expressed in the CeA-PKCδ neurons, which exhibited enhanced excitability relative to the CeA-SST neurons.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: In a neuropathic pain model, chemogenetic silencing of CeA-PKCδ neurons or activation of CeA-SST neurons reversed nerve-injury-induced hyperalgesia.
claims.source: Furthermore, chemogenetic silencing of CeA-PKCδ neurons or activation of the CeA-SST neurons reversed nerve-injury-induced hyperalgesia (Wilson et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: Chemogenetic inhibition of CeA-PKCδ neurons reduced mechanical hyperalgesia in mice with formalin-induced pain.
claims.source: Similarly, another study demonstrated that chemogenetic inhibition of the CeA-PKCδ neurons reduced mechanical hyperalgesia in mice with formalin-induced pain (Chen et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: Using the spared nerve injury model, a small population of CeA-SST neurons that are glutamatergic and project to the lateral habenula exhibited enhanced excitability and were involved in a neural circuit for hyperalgesia and comorbid depressive symptoms.
claims.source: Using the spared nerve injury model, Zhou and colleagues demonstrated that a small population of CeA-SST neurons, which are glutamatergic and project to the lateral habenula (LHb), exhibited enhanced excitability and were involved in a neural circuit for hyperalgesia and comorbid depressive symptoms (Zhou et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: A subpopulation of neurons co-expressing PKCδ and enkephalin confined to the mid-posterior axis of the CeA mediates antinociceptive function in response to general anesthetics.
claims.source: Moreover, a subpopulation of neurons co-expressing PKCδ and enkephalin confined to the mid-posterior axis of the CeA was shown to mediate the antinociceptive function in response to general anesthetics (Hua et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: The subtype of sensitized neurons in the central nucleus of the amygdala may vary based on the chronic pain models.
claims.source: Overall, the subtype of sensitized neurons in the CeA may vary based on the chronic pain models.
claims.evidence: This statement is an inference based on the comparison of different studies showing different results in different pain models.

claims.claim: CeA-SST neurons contain heterogeneous subpopulations.
claims.source: Our results support a notion that the CeA-SST neurons contain heterogeneous subpopulations (Penzo et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research and is consistent with the current findings.

claims.claim: CeA-SST neurons comprise at least two distinct subtypes of pro-nociceptive neurons based on their intrinsic firing properties and downstream targets in the muscle pain model.
claims.source: The CeA-SST neurons could comprise at least two distinct subtypes of pro-nociceptive neurons based on their intrinsic firing properties and downstream targets in the MP model.
claims.evidence: This statement is speculative based on the observation that silencing CeA-SST neurons affects both pain and affect.

claims.claim: A subset of CeA-SST neurons could project onto the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis for approach-avoidance behavior, the midbrain ventrolateral periaqueductal gray for active-avoidance behavior, and the lateral habenula for depression-like behavior.
claims.source: A subset of the CeA-SST neurons could project onto the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis for approach-avoidance behavior, the midbrain ventrolateral periaqueductal gray for active-avoidance behavior, and the LHb for depression-like behavior.
claims.evidence: This statement is speculative based on known projections of CeA-SST neurons from prior research.

claims.claim: CeA-PKCδ neurons could inhibit another subset of CeA-SST neurons that form reciprocal inhibition with CeA-PKCδ neurons.
claims.source: We speculate that the CeA-PKCδ neurons could inhibit the other subset of the CeA-SST neurons, which form reciprocal inhibition with the CeA-PKCδ neurons.
claims.evidence: This statement is speculative based on known circuit architecture.

claims.claim: Chemogenetic activation of CeA-PKCδ neurons reduced tactile allodynia without influencing affective behaviors in muscle pain.
claims.source: In agreement with this hypothesis, chemogenetic activation of CeA-PKCδ neurons reduced tactile allodynia without influencing affective behaviors in MP.

results.result: The acid-induced muscle pain model requires two acidic saline injections (day 0 and day 3) to produce sustained bilateral mechanical hypersensitivity lasting at least 14 days, while control mice receiving neutral saline show no changes in paw withdrawal threshold.
results.evaluation: Claims C13-C15, C25-C28, C102-C103 collectively establish the muscle pain model with strong experimental support from Figure 1A-C and citations to prior work. The data clearly demonstrate sustained bilateral mechanical hypersensitivity in MP mice versus controls, validating the model's face validity for chronic musculoskeletal pain.

results.result: Muscle pain mice exhibit anxiety-like and depression-like behaviors including reduced open-arm time in EPM, fewer light-dark transitions, increased marble burying, increased immobility in FST, and reduced sociability, without changes in locomotion.
results.evaluation: Claims C29-C35 are well-supported by behavioral data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-E. The consistent demonstration of affective comorbidities across multiple validated behavioral assays, with appropriate locomotion controls, provides strong evidence for the model's construct validity.

results.result: Local infusion of pregabalin into the CeA either during established chronic pain (days 16-19) or during the priming phase (day 3) reduces mechanical allodynia and prevents pain chronification.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C39, C41-C42, C104-C105 are strongly supported by experimental data in Figures 1E-F. The demonstration that PGB is effective both therapeutically and preventatively provides robust evidence for CeA involvement in pain chronification, establishing predictive validity.

results.result: Intra-CeA pregabalin infusion alleviates anxiety-like and depression-like behaviors in muscle pain mice without affecting locomotion or behaviors in control mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C48 are supported by behavioral data in Figures 2B-E showing that PGB selectively improves affective behaviors in MP mice across multiple assays (EPM, marble burying, FST, sociability) with appropriate controls demonstrating specificity and lack of locomotor effects.

results.result: Pregabalin infusion during the priming phase (day 3) prevents the development of chronic pain-related affective symptoms.
results.evaluation: Claims C49-C53 are supported by behavioral data in Figures 2G-J demonstrating that early PGB intervention during hyperalgesic priming prevents both pain and affective comorbidities, providing strong evidence for a critical window during pain chronification.

results.result: Muscle pain is associated with increased sEPSC and mEPSC frequency (but not amplitude) in CeA-SST neurons and decreased frequency in CeA-PKCδ neurons, indicating strengthened excitatory transmission onto CeA-SST neurons and weakened transmission onto CeA-PKCδ neurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C60, C106-C107 are well-supported by electrophysiological data in Figures 3C-D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B. The consistent changes in frequency without amplitude changes across both sEPSCs and mEPSCs provide strong evidence for presynaptic alterations in excitatory transmission.

results.result: CeA-SST neurons show enhanced intrinsic excitability in muscle pain mice (increased spike numbers, lower rheobase) while CeA-PKCδ neurons show decreased excitability, without changes in resting membrane potential or input resistance.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C67, C108-C109 are supported by electrophysiological data in Figures 3E-H and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C-F. The bidirectional changes in excitability between CeA-SST and CeA-PKCδ neurons, with preserved passive membrane properties, indicate cell-type-specific intrinsic plasticity.

results.result: The number of pERK-positive cells is increased in the CeA of muscle pain mice, with the increase predominantly in CeA-SST neurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C68-C69 are supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-D showing increased pERK expression in MP mice with preferential localization to CeA-SST neurons, providing molecular evidence for SST neuron activation in chronic pain.

results.result: Chemogenetic silencing of CeA-SST neurons during the priming phase (day 3) prevents the development of chronic muscle pain, demonstrating that CeA-SST neuron activation is necessary for pain chronification.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C70-C73 are strongly supported by data in Figures 4C1-C2 and 4D. The validation of hM4Di function ex vivo and the prevention of chronic pain development by CNO-mediated silencing during priming provide compelling causal evidence for CeA-SST neuron involvement.

results.result: Chemogenetic inactivation of CeA-SST neurons in established chronic pain reduces mechanical hyperalgesia and alleviates anxiety-like and depression-like behaviors without affecting control mice or locomotion.
results.evaluation: Claims C8, C74-C83, C110 are comprehensively supported by behavioral data in Figures 4E-J and Figure 4—figure supplement 3. The selective improvement of both pain and affective symptoms in MP mice, with appropriate controls, demonstrates the therapeutic potential of targeting CeA-SST neurons.

results.result: Chemogenetic activation of CeA-PKCδ neurons reduces mechanical hyperalgesia but does not affect anxiety-like or depression-like behaviors, indicating that CeA-PKCδ neurons modulate pain but not affective symptoms.
results.evaluation: Claims C84-C90, C145 are supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 4C-I showing that hM3Dq activation of CeA-PKCδ neurons selectively reduces pain without affecting multiple affective behavioral measures, demonstrating functional dissociation between pain and affect circuits.

results.result: Pregabalin suppresses excitatory synaptic transmission at PBN-to-CeA-SST and PBN-to-CeA-PKCδ synapses through a presynaptic mechanism (increased paired-pulse ratio), with a higher percentage of PGB-sensitive neurons in muscle pain mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C9, C91-C95, C101, C111 are well-supported by optogenetic electrophysiology data in Figures 5B-E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1. The demonstration of presynaptic PGB effects with increased sensitivity in MP mice provides a clear mechanism for PGB's therapeutic action.

results.result: In vivo calcium imaging shows that systemic pregabalin injection decreases calcium event frequency and amplitude in approximately 56% of CeA-SST neurons, while 11% are excited and 33% are insensitive.
results.evaluation: Claims C96-C100 are supported by in vivo calcium imaging data in Figures 5G-J. The demonstration of heterogeneous PGB responses in CeA-SST neurons in freely moving mice provides important evidence for functional diversity within this population.

results.result: The effects of pregabalin on pain threshold and emotional behaviors may be mediated by distinct circuit mechanisms, as evidenced by lack of correlation between pain reduction and immobility time changes, and only weak correlation with marble burying.
results.evaluation: Claims C112-C115 are based on correlation analyses in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-B showing dissociation between pain and affect measures. However, the interpretation is speculative and the weak/absent correlations could reflect measurement variability, different time courses, or ceiling/floor effects rather than distinct mechanisms. Additional experiments would be needed to definitively establish separate circuits.

results.result: The PBN-to-CeA-SST synapse shows no significant changes in EPSC amplitude or paired-pulse ratio in muscle pain mice, suggesting that other inputs (possibly from PVT or BLA) contribute to the increased spontaneous synaptic events in CeA-SST neurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C124-C129 are supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 2 and citations to prior work. The lack of changes at PBN-CeA-SST synapses, combined with increased sEPSC frequency, logically suggests involvement of other excitatory inputs, though direct evidence for PVT/BLA contributions in this model is not provided.

results.result: Analysis of early-spiking (ES) versus late-spiking (LS) subtypes reveals that enhanced excitatory transmission in muscle pain is specific to CeA-SST-ES neurons and depressed transmission is specific to CeA-PKCδ-LS neurons, while excitability changes are specific to ES neurons in both populations.
results.evaluation: Claims C147-C150 are supported by detailed electrophysiological analysis in Figure 3—figure supplement 4. This subtype-specific analysis provides important evidence for functional heterogeneity within molecularly defined populations, though the functional significance of ES/LS subtypes requires further investigation.

results.result: ERK signaling may contribute to increased intrinsic excitability of CeA-SST neurons through the CaMKII-PKA/PKC-ERK-CREB pathway, which can regulate ion channel expression and alter action potential threshold.
results.evaluation: Claims C130-C134 are largely speculative, based on the observation of increased pERK in CeA-SST neurons (C68-C69) and citations to prior research on ERK signaling pathways. While the proposed mechanism is plausible and well-grounded in the literature, direct experimental evidence linking ERK activity to the observed excitability changes in this model is not provided.

results.result: CeA-SST neurons comprise heterogeneous subpopulations that may include at least two distinct subtypes with different projection targets (BNST, vlPAG, LHb for one subtype; reciprocal connections with PKCδ neurons for another) mediating different aspects of pain and affect.
results.evaluation: Claims C141-C144 are speculative interpretations based on the dissociation between pain and affect observed with CeA-SST versus CeA-PKCδ manipulations. While the hypothesis is reasonable and consistent with prior anatomical studies cited, direct evidence for these specific projection patterns and their functional roles in this model is not provided.

results.result: Single molecular markers (SST or PKCδ) may be insufficient for identifying functionally distinct CeA populations; composite molecular markers, anatomical locations, and physiological properties should be considered for more specific targeting.
results.evaluation: Claims C146, C151-C157 represent a critical self-assessment of the study's methodology, supported by the observed heterogeneity in responses and citations to prior work showing anatomical and physiological diversity within molecularly defined populations. This is an important caveat that appropriately acknowledges limitations.

They accurately represent prior knowledge and set up the rationale for the current investigation.
